summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token usage, and production systems can typically reduce spend by 50-80% through a combination of prompt optimization, caching, and intelligent model routing without sacrificing output quality. Prompt caching alone cuts input costs by up to 90% on repeated context, while semantic caching achieves hit rates near 68% in real workloads. Because these techniques compound, teams can often lower a $10K monthly bill to $2K while also improving latency.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Cache static or repeated portions of a prompt (system instructions, few-shot examples, long documents) so the provider does not re-process them on every request. Most providers charge a fraction of the input rate for cached tokens.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Mark a long system prompt and shared document context as cacheable with Anthropic's cache_control blocks so subsequent calls only pay full price for the new user message.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store LLM responses keyed by the embedding of the input so semantically similar queries return cached answers instead of hitting the model. Uses a vector similarity threshold to decide cache hits.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to serve the same answer for 'How do I reset my password?' and 'What's the password reset process?' without a new model call.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route simple requests to small, cheap models and escalate only hard requests to larger, expensive ones. A cheaper model answers first and a confidence check or validator decides whether to escalate.
techniques.example: Send classification tasks to GPT-4o-mini and only fall back to GPT-4o when the mini model returns low confidence or fails a validation check.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim verbose instructions, redundant examples, and filler language from prompts, and compress long context using summarization or tools like LLMLingua. Fewer input tokens directly lower cost and latency.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-token multi-paragraph instruction with a concise 150-token version, or run context through LLMLingua to compress a long document before sending.

techniques.name: Max Token & Output Length Control
techniques.description: Set max_tokens limits and instruct the model to be concise so it does not generate unnecessarily long outputs. Output tokens are often priced higher than input tokens.
techniques.example: Add 'Respond in under 3 sentences' to the prompt and set max_tokens=150 for a summarization endpoint instead of allowing unbounded generation.

techniques.name: Structured Output & Function Calling
techniques.description: Request compact structured formats (JSON schema, enums) instead of free-form prose to minimize generated tokens and avoid costly reformatting calls.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI structured outputs with a strict JSON schema so the model returns {"sentiment":"positive"} rather than a paragraph explaining the sentiment.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single call or use provider batch APIs that offer discounted asynchronous processing. Reduces per-request overhead and unit cost.
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 classification jobs to OpenAI's Batch API overnight at 50% off instead of making real-time synchronous calls.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Context Trimming (RAG)
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into the prompt, retrieve and inject only the most relevant chunks via vector search. Keeps context small and relevant.
techniques.example: Retrieve the top 3 relevant knowledge-base passages for a support question rather than passing the full 50-page manual on every request.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed answer or stop sequence is produced, avoiding paying for trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '</answer>' so the model halts immediately after producing the structured result rather than continuing to explain.

techniques.name: Open-Source / Self-Hosted Model Substitution
techniques.description: Serve high-volume or low-complexity workloads on self-hosted open models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) to eliminate per-token API fees entirely at scale.
techniques.example: Host Llama 3.1 8B on vLLM for internal document classification instead of paying GPT-4o per-token rates for millions of daily calls.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores and retrieves LLM responses using embedding similarity to cut repeated calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (self-hosted infra costs only)

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used to build fast exact and semantic caches for LLM responses and embeddings.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo; Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Enterprise tier custom pricing; OSS is free

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, caching, rate limiting, and cost analytics via a proxy.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite), prompt templating, and RAG primitives.
tools.pricing_paid: LangSmith paid plans from ~$39/mo per seat; framework is free

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that reduces prompt length while preserving meaning to lower input token costs.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, load balancing, fallbacks, and cost/usage observability across providers.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine with PagedAttention for efficient self-hosted serving of open models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (GPU/infra costs only)

tools.name: Ollama
tools.description: Tool for running open-source LLMs locally or on-prem with a simple API, useful for eliminating API token costs.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API aggregating many model providers with automatic routing and price comparison to pick cheaper models.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go per token with small routing margin

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for static system prompts and shared context to cut repeated input costs by up to 90%.
Trim verbose prompts and set max_tokens limits to immediately reduce both input and output token spend.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to serve repeated/similar queries for free.
Route simple requests to a cheaper small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only escalate hard cases to larger models.
Move high-volume, non-urgent jobs to provider batch APIs for an instant ~50% discount.
